topic: Context Compression for AI Coding Agents: Frameworks Compared in 2026

competitors.title: AI Agent Context Compression: Strategies for Long-Running Sessions
key_points: Context drift kills agents before context limits do — 65% of enterprise AI failures in 2025 attributed to context drift or memory loss
Anchored iterative summarization outperforms full-reconstruction: Factory's evaluation across 36,000 engineering session messages showed higher accuracy, completeness, and continuity
ACON reduces memory usage 26-54% while preserving 95%+ task accuracy via failure-driven guideline optimization
Anthropic's compaction API (compact-2026-01-12) provides production-ready automatic compaction across Claude API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry
Industry shifting from expanding context windows to smarter context management — window size plateauing as focus shifts to inference-time scaling and hybrid compression+caching
Six compression approaches: sliding window, rolling LLM summarization, anchored iterative summarization, ACON, provider-native compaction, and embedding-based compression
Recommended compression ratios: conversation history 3:1-5:1, tool outputs 10:1-20:1, recent messages no compression, system prompt never compressed
Trigger compaction when context utilization exceeds 70% of available budget

competitors.title: LLM Context Window Comparison 2026: GPT-4o vs Claude vs Gemini
key_points: Context windows grew 2,500x in three years — from GPT-3's 4K tokens in 2023 to Qwen Long's 10M tokens in 2026
Coding agents burn through 150K+ tokens per session without compression, prohibitive at Claude Opus pricing above the 200K cliff
200K pricing cliff: Anthropic and Google charge 2x standard input rate when request exceeds 200K tokens, applied to ALL tokens
At 1B tokens/month input, costs range from $100 (Gemini Flash-Lite) to $5,000 (Claude Opus 4.6) — a 35x spread
Context rot: every model tested shows performance degradation as context length increases — Gemini 1.5 Pro loses only -2.3 RULER points from 4K to 128K, GPT-4 drops -15.4 points
RAG vs long context: use long context for reasoning-heavy single documents, RAG for factual retrieval across large corpora, context compression in agentic sessions to stay below pricing cliffs
Compression of 50%+ achievable without meaningful quality loss, halving context window consumption per session

competitors.title: Context Engineering 2026: Complete Developer Guide
key_points: Context engineering is the discipline of designing and managing the information in a model's context window — coined by Andrej Karpathy in mid-2025
Agents now complete average of 20 autonomous actions before requiring human input (Anthropic 2026 Agentic Coding Trends Report)
95% of professional developers use AI tools weekly
Peer-reviewed study across 9,649 experiments: context quality is a stronger predictor of output quality than prompt quality
Six layers of context engineering: system prompt architecture, RAG, tool/function selection, memory systems, context compression, information ordering
Progressive summarization: replace oldest turns with structured summary after every N exchanges — reduces total input token consumption 40-60% across a session
Practical rule: when context is more than 60% full and more than a few steps remain, start compressing
At Claude Opus 4.7 pricing of $5/M tokens, a 20-step session costing $20 in input tokens without compression might cost $8-12 with compression

competitors.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Complete 2026 Guide
key_points: Google DeepMind's Philipp Schmid: 'Most agent failures are not model failures anymore, they are context failures'

Four failure modes: context poisoning (hallucinations treated as facts), context distraction (fixating on irrelevant history), context confusion (conflicting retrieved documents), context clash (contradictory information)
LangChain's Deep Agents harness: three-tier compression — offload tool responses >20K tokens to filesystem, truncate file inputs at 85% context, generate structured summary when neither is enough
Semantic compression can reduce token usage by 50-80% while preserving needed information
Anthropic's data: sessions stopping at 75% context utilization produce higher-quality, more maintainable output
Isolation pattern: delegate subtasks to separate agents with clean context windows — parent receives only output, not full working memory
Four-tier memory model: working memory (zero latency, volatile), short-term (low latency, session), long-term (medium, cross-session), permanent (archival)
